sections.changelog:
Fixed

  • **A Plus written on the modifier is now read as one.** The variant rule knew the sign only where it sits on the number ("J6+"), and a catalogue writes it on the modifier just as readily — "Redmi Note 12 Pro+", "Tab S10 FE+", "Realme 9 Pro+" — where it went unseen and the Pro+ parts became indistinguishable from the Pro ones. They are different devices whose displays and frames do not interchange, and the damage fell on the plain query: measured on a 12 460-product parts shop, "redmi note 12 pro" returned eight of its first ten as Pro+ parts, "realme 9 pro" three of ten; with the sign read they return one and none, and the Pro+ parts stay on the page, just below. 154 of that shop's titles carry the sign this way. The query side reads it through a space as well, because that is how it is typed — of the plus-bearing queries in the shop's log one was written "realme 12 pro +" — while a title keeps a spaced "+" as the list of what else is in the box ("Realme 9 Pro + OCA", 1 168 titles), which is why the two sides read it differently. What may stand before the sign stays narrow — a digit or a known modifier — and what may follow it narrower still: a letter or a digit behind the sign means it belongs to a code, so "68+E" and "HB444199EBC+ (Honor 4C)" are left alone. A modifier the list does not carry ("S6 Edge+") is still invisible; the `mvweb_ss_model_qualifiers` filter takes catalogue-specific ones.
